content.value: The Capabilities Manifest — `GET /v1/capabilities` — is a tier-keyed self-description that teaches the entire API in one call and builds the bp CLI from itself.

returns a machine-readable description of everything Barkpark can do: the Schemas, the field types from Schema v2, the available Datasets and Perspectives, the mutation verbs, and the graph verbs. A client never has to hardcode endpoints — it reads the manifest and learns the HTTP API v1 surface dynamically.

: what it lists depends on the caller's Auth and Tokens tier. A low-tier token sees a smaller surface; existence of higher-tier verbs is hidden rather than merely forbidden, so the manifest doubles as an access-control map scoped within Workspace + Project.
— it constructs its own commands and flags from
rather than shipping a baked-in command table. Add a verb server-side and the CLI gains it on next sync. The same is true for graph operations: the manifest lists the graph verbs
learns to query the Content Graph for an Orphan Node or a Dangling Reference without bespoke wiring.

Served by the Phoenix API and catalogued under API and Contracts, the manifest is the canonical self-description — where the JS SDK and Go TUI discover what a Document looks like. Because every surface reads it at runtime, it is the single source that keeps them all in sync with the Content Model. New Plugins endpoints appear in it automatically, so clients gain plugin commands with no recompile.
